newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa approves separation of central bank roles.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa approves separation of central bank roles.

text.p: Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said the South African cabinet had on Wednesday approved measures to separate the market-making role of the Reserve Bank from its regulatory functions.
Manuel told a news conference after the regular weekly cabinet meeting that management of debt, cash and assets would be revamped to generate substantial savings.

"Cabinet approved firstly to ring fence all the funding activities that are currently being performed by the Reserve Bank on behalf of the department of finance from the monetary activities of the Reserve Bank," Manuel said.
He said the central bank would be made directly accountable to the ministry of finance on all matters concerning debt management within its proposed risk management principles.
The move would not affect the bank's independence in setting monetary policy, he said.

"The interaction with market participants will be continued with a view to appointing a number of primary dealers in such a way that the risk of market making be shifted from the Reserve Bank to the primary dealers," Manuel said.
"The bank has been both market maker and monetary authority, (posing a) very serious risk of conflict, and so that separation is important."
The government first proposed discontinuing making a market in its own debt in March last year as part of restructuring its overall debt management.
Manuel said mechanisms would be implemented to ensure the government had adequate sums of cash available "in the right place, at the right time and in the right currencies".
